title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68) comparing ungated LLM generation (baseline) to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline. Generation used gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial-generation protocol (one candidate per intent shared by both arms). The guarded arm validated the shared candidate with a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and applied ≤1 deterministic repair iteration when the validator reported repairable faults. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline emulator-executable successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary test used the exact McNemar two-sided (binomial) formulation (discordant counts n10=1, n01=0) yielding p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We report the validator checks, the deterministic repair heuristics and invocation rule, the exact statistical implementation for small discordant counts, and operational limitations (shared-generation estimand, synthetic tasks, single LLM, bounded repair budget, emulator fidelity). All experimental artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) tasks with generative large language models (LLMs) promises efficiency but raises reliability and safety concerns: LLMs can produce syntactically plausible yet operationally unsafe or incomplete configurations (incorrect ordering, omitted prerequisites, or protected-interface violations). Prior work proposes verifier-augmented and repair architectures to reduce such failures, but rigorous, execution-grounded evidence measuring their marginal efficacy is limited. We preregistered a narrowly scoped paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard raises the proportion of emulator-executable configurations relative to accepting ungated LLM outputs. To isolate deterministic repair-on-same-candidate efficacy, we used a shared-initial-generation protocol: a single candidate per intent was produced and fed to both the ungated baseline and the guarded validator/repair flow. Our contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired evaluation (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) reporting exact paired counts, a small-discordant-count inferential treatment, a concise algorithmic description of the deterministic repair operator used in the guarded arm, and an evidence-grounded discussion of operational implications and validity threats.
sections.related_work: Surveys and prototype studies document LLM applications to intent-to-configuration translation and co-pilot assistance while reporting hallucinations and schema violations as recurring failure modes [doi:10.1002/nem.2313; https://openalex.org/W7161165783]. Cross-domain mitigation techniques include retrieval-augmented generation, constrained decoding, live schema grounding and verifier-assisted repair loops; these reduce but do not eliminate structured-output errors [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6909831]. Formal-method verifiers such as NetKAT variants and ensemble verifiers can detect reachability and isolation violations and serve as natural validators for generated network configurations, but they face fidelity and scalability trade-offs when modeling control-plane dynamics [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Adversarial prompt studies emphasize that unconstrained generation is vulnerable to manipulations relevant for operational pipelines [doi:10.1145/3815174]. Our study complements these works by measuring the incremental effect of a bounded, deterministic repair stage applied to an identical shared candidate rather than evaluating architectures that permit independent re-sampling or repeated LLM calls.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental design: the study was preregistered and frozen prior to execution (preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd...ff68). Confirmatory sample: n=200 natural-language change intents curated to span single-device and small multi-device changes (ACLs, VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns). Paired estimand and protocol: shared-initial-generation with one LLM candidate per intent shared by both arms; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Model, budget, and execution: declared model gpt-5-mini; maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized hosted-model calls used = 201. Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Outcome definition: an episode is successful when the deterministic validator reports validation_after.valid == true when the candidate configuration is applied to the emulator. Missingness and retries: single automatic retry for transient provider/API errors (60s backoff); provider/API failures are counted as failures in the primary analysis (no such failures occurred).
sections.results: Execution accounting and primary outcome: the run completed 400 episodes (200 paired intents) with zero provider/API failures; hosted-model calls used = 201 (shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). Artifact-backed primary counts: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). The observed paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Deterministic repair and failure accounting: an initial validator failure (validation_before.valid == false) occurred in exactly one episode; syntactic parse failures = 0; deterministic repair invocations = 1 (the single repair converted that validator-failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success). Missingness: no missing or unscorable episodes were recorded in the confirmatory analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).
sections.discussion: Statistical inference and its small-discordant-count implementation: the preregistered primary hypothesis test used the exact McNemar two-sided formulation implemented via a binomial test on discordant counts. Under the null that discordant directions are equally likely, the number of pairs observed in one direction (here n10) is Binomial(n = n10 + n01, p = 0.5). With observed n10 = 1 and n01 = 0, the two-sided exact p-value computed from this binomial formulation equals 1.0 (artifact: analysis/results.json). Complementary uncertainty quantification used paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729), yielding [0.0, 0.015] (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The near-ceiling baseline (0.995) diverged from preregistered power assumptions (baseline ≈0.50 and target absolute effect 0.15) and materially reduced the study’s sensitivity to large absolute improvements; the observed CI excludes effects ≥0.015 and hence excludes the preregistered 0.15 effect given the realized distribution.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to evaluate a bounded generate–verify–repair guard for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The artifact-backed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]), excluding the preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect because of the realized near-ceiling baseline. For the confirmatory distribution and estimand studied, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded a negligible marginal improvement; broader operational value depends on task difficulty, estimand choice (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling), model capability, repair budget, and emulator fidelity. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multivendor CLI diversity, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and enhanced emulator fidelity (control-plane timing) to better characterize when GVR guards provide substantive operational benefits.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (declared in execution/model_configuration.json); validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' recorded in scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; provider-call stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1. All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolates repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Aggregate task-difficulty metadata (easy / medium / hard / very_hard) for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; manifest hash recorded in the execution manifest) and may be inspected in the evidence bundle for per-task difficulty counts; the archived manifest contains these per-task labels but a preregistered focus on paired success outcomes led to not aggregating those counts in the original analysis artifacts.
